name: Do I need to replace the bathroom fan during a remodel?

mainEntity.name: Should a bathroom exhaust fan be replaced during a renovation even if it still works?
mainEntity.text: Should a bathroom exhaust fan be replaced during a renovation even if it still works?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even if an old fan still runs, it may not be enough for a remodeled bathroom. Modern bathrooms often have better sealing, larger showers, and more moisture-producing fixtures, so ventilation demands can increase. A noisy or weak fan is worth replacing during renovation because access is already open and the labor overlap is efficient. The most important factors are proper sizing, quiet operation, and correct ducted venting to the exterior. If the bathroom has had mildew or condensation problems, upgrading the fan is one of the highest-value decisions you can make. Ask the contractor to confirm fan capacity, duct route, and switch control before the walls are closed up. That small step can prevent a lot of future moisture trouble.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replacing the bathroom fan during a remodel is often a smart move if the existing unit is noisy, underpowered, or vented poorly. A good fan helps prevent condensation, mildew, and hidden moisture damage, especially in a tightly sealed modern bathroom.
